title: Local context priority & pinning — personal design notes
body:
Purpose:

This is a personal working draft describing an approach to let client SDKs signal local-context priorities and "soft pin" hints to the runtime so we can: 1) keep hot context on-device, 2) reduce round trips for small continuity tokens, and 3) gather telemetry to validate cost/quality tradeoffs. Not a final spec — collecting design options + concrete API shapes for experimentation.

Problem statement / motivation:
- Many product flows have a small amount of high-value context (recent user messages, short preference vectors, metadata) that matters for quality but is expensive to rehydrate every request.
- Server-only caching has higher latency and cost; full local persistence is heavyweight and inconsistent between clients.
- We need a way for SDKs (mobile/desktop/web) to indicate which pieces of context are worth keeping locally and how strongly to prefer keeping them.

Goals (ranked):
1) Lightweight developer-facing API to express priority without leaking internal runtime details.
2) Predictable cost/latency impact — allow the runtime to estimate savings.
3) Telemetry hooks to measure hit-rate vs. quality regressions.
4) Safe defaults (no user secrets pinned by accident).
5) Experimentation-friendly: flags to toggle hard vs soft behavior.

Assumptions / constraints:
- Clients may be offline or have intermittent connectivity.
- Local pin budget must be bounded by tokens/size and be revocable by server policy.
- Privacy: pinned payloads must exclude PII unless explicitly consented and encrypted with customer-managed keys.

Key concepts / vocabulary:
- hint: small metadata blob attached to a request describing candidate context for local pinning.
- soft pin: suggestion to keep something cached locally; runtime may evict under pressure.
- hard pin: elevated suggestion that should be respected unless explicit eviction command. (Use sparingly.)
- grace window: time after last use where a soft pin is treated as recently used and less likely to be evicted.
- prefetch score: runtime-computed score indicating estimated benefit of keeping object locally.

High-level flow (ASCII diagram):

Client SDK --> (1) Request + hints --> Runtime / Gateway --> (2) Decision: pin / prefetch / noop --> Local cache manager (client or edge)

                +-----------------+       +----------------+    +----------------------+
Client SDK --->| Request + Hints  |------>| Gateway/Router |--->| Runtime cache policy  |
                +-----------------+       +----------------+    +----------------------+
                                                              |                       |
                                                              v                       v
                                                      local cache add            telemetry event

API shapes — hint envelope (client -> server):

{
  "priority_hint": {
    "hint_id": "string (uuid)",
    "items": [
      { "key": "conversation_ctx_v2", "size_bytes": 1024, "type": "kv", "ttl_seconds": 3600, "importance": "high" },
      { "key": "user_short_profile", "size_bytes": 256, "type": "json", "ttl_seconds": 86400, "importance": "medium" }
    ],
    "intent": "continuity|prefetch|telemetry_only",
    "origin": "sdk|edge|plugin",
    "signature": "optional HMAC for server-authenticated hints"
  }
}

Notes on fields:
- key: opaque identifier for the context blob. Server should not assume format.
- size_bytes: helps estimate budget impact.
- ttl_seconds: client preference for freshness.
- importance: enum {low, medium, high}. Maps to policy weights.
- intent: informs whether this is just a telemetry signal or a hard expectation to prefetch.

Server -> Client response (when gateway elects to prefetch/pin):

{
  "pin_decision": {
    "hint_id": "uuid",
    "verdict": "noop|soft_pin|hard_pin|prefetch_immediate",
    "estimated_unit_savings": "float tokens/savings_estimate",
    "revocation_handle": "string (for explicit evictions)",
    "policy_version": "vX.Y"
  }
}

Local cache config (client-side SDK config JSON example):

{
  "local_cache": {
    "max_bytes": 524288,    // default 512KB
    "max_entries": 500,
    "pin_budget": 64,       // max number of hard pins
    "eviction_policy": "lru_weighted", // weighted by importance+age
    "aging_multiplier": 0.75,
    "grace_window_seconds": 300
  }
}

Eviction scoring (sketch):
score = base_age_penalty * (1 - recency_score) + size_penalty * log(size_bytes) - importance_bonus
where importance_bonus = {low:1, medium:3, high:7} * policy_weight.

Telemetry / observability (minimum events to emit):
- hint_submitted {hint_id, items_count, origin, client_platform, request_path}
- pin_decision {hint_id, verdict, policy_version, estimated_savings}
- local_cache_hit {key, hint_id?, latency_ms}
- local_cache_miss {key, hint_id?, miss_reason}
- eviction_event {key, reason, policy_version, estimate_loss}
- quality_regression_alert {experiment_id, prompt_set_id, delta_metric}
Telemetry hints: include sampling flags and non-PII aggregated buckets. Attach SDK-version to every event.

Experimentation plan:
- Phase A (opt-in): runtime honors hints only for telemetry; clients send hints and we collect hit/miss and quality correlation.
- Phase B (soft pin): runtime returns soft_pin verdicts and clients keep locally under budget. Monitor unit-cost and latency.
- Phase C (hard pin / prefetch): experiment small % of traffic where prefetch happens immediately for high-importance items.

Edge cases & open questions:
- Should pinned blobs be encrypted with customer KMS keys on mobile? (pro: privacy; con: complexity)
- Revocation semantics when server policy changes mid-flight. Need revocation_handle + forced fetch to flush stale pins.
- How to avoid clients hoarding space (malicious SDKs)? Need per-client budget tied to API key or device id and server-side enforcement.
- Format negotiation: server must accept opaque keys but provide a mechanism to explain cost (size/type) without revealing user data.

Security note:
- Default policy: node will never instruct to pin anything marked as sensitive by the SDK (explicit sensitive flag). SDKs should perform a first-pass scrubbing; server policy adds a second layer.

Developer ergonomics / SDK surfaces:
- Minimal API: attachPriorityHints(hints, options) on request builder.
- Optional callback: onPinDecision(decision, meta) for apps to surface to UX or metrics.
- CLI tool to inspect local cache contents for debugging (local-only; must opt-in).

Small toy example (flow):
- Messaging app: user sends message A, then message B. SDK attaches hint for `conversation_ctx_v2` after B with importance=high.
- Gateway returns soft_pin. Client retains 1KB of recent tokens locally. Next request hits local cache and saves 1-2 RTTs. Telemetry logs hit and estimated_token_savings.

Open TODOs for next pass:
- Define exact protobuf/REST shapes and minimal wire encoding for hints to keep payload tiny.
- Run bench: simulate client budgets (512KB, 256KB) and measure hit rate on representative conversation traffic.
- Draft server-side policy weights and rollout knob (percent of population).

Notes to self:
- Avoid coupling hint keys to model internals; treat keys as SDK-generated opaque ids.
- Keep initial API as additive (telemetry-only) so we can gather fallback-safe signals.

References / inspiration:
- local cache papers (offline-first UX)
- prior Redwood work on KV cache and prefix caching (see confluence page linked above)

If/when we move this to a formal RFC, include concrete schema, security checklist, and retrofitting plan for existing SDKs. For now: collect feedback from Jonas, Priya, and SRE on revocation/telemetry volume."
